questions.text:
Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{R}$ be such that the system of linear equations
$$\begin{array}{l}
x+2 y+z=5 \\
2 x+y+\alpha z=5 \\
8 x+4 y+\beta z=18
\end{array}$$
has no solution. Then $\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is equal to :
(1) -4
(2) 4
(3) 8
(4) -8

steps:
$\mathrm{x}+2 \mathrm{y}+\mathrm{z}=5$
$$\begin{array}{l}
2 x+y+\alpha z=5 \\
8 x+4 y+\beta z=18
\end{array}$$
for no solution
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta=\left|\begin{array}{lll}
1 & 2 & 1 \\
2 & 1 & \alpha \\
8 & 4 & \beta
\end{array}\right|=0 \\
\Delta=1(\beta-4 \alpha)-2(2 \beta-8 \alpha)+1(0)=0 \\
=\beta-4 \alpha-4 \beta+16 \alpha=0 \\
\Rightarrow 4 \alpha=\beta
\end{array}$$

For point of intersection
$$\begin{array}{l}
3 r_{1}-1=r_{2}+2 \Rightarrow r_{2}=3 r_{1}-3 \\
5 r_{1}-a=4 r_{2}+b \\
7 r_{1}-b-1=7 r_{2}+2 a
\end{array}$$

Since point lies on XY plane
$$\Rightarrow \mathrm{z}-\text { coordinate }=0$$

From $\mathrm{L}_{1}: 7 \mathrm{r}_{1}-\mathrm{b}-1=0 \Rightarrow 7 \mathrm{r}_{1}=\mathrm{b}+1$
From $\mathrm{L}_{2}: 7 \mathrm{r}_{2}+2 \mathrm{a}=0 \Rightarrow 2 \mathrm{a}=-7 \mathrm{r}_{2}$

questions.text:
If $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}$ are two vectors such that $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}|=2$ and $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{b}}|=3$, then the maximum value of $3|(3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}+2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}})|+4|(3 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{a}}-2 \overrightarrow{\mathrm{~b}})|$ is :
(1) 30
(2) 36
(3) 60
(4)

steps:
$$\begin{array}{l}
E=3 \sqrt{9 a^{2}+4 b^{2}+12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}+4 \sqrt{9 a^{2}+4 b^{2}-12 \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}} \\
=3 \sqrt{36+36+12 \times 6 \cos \theta}+4 \sqrt{36+36-72 \cos \theta} \\
=3 \sqrt{72+72 \cos \theta}+4 \sqrt{72-72 \cos \theta} \\
=18 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{1+\cos \theta}+24 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{1-\cos \theta} \\
=18 \sqrt{2} \sqrt{2} \cos \frac{\theta}{2}+24 \sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{2} \sin \frac{\theta}{2}\right) \\
=36\left(\cos \frac{\theta}{2}\right)+48 \sin \left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) \\
E_{\max }=\sqrt{(36)^{2}+(48)^{2}}=\sqrt{6^{4}+6^{2} \times 8^{2}}=60

questions.text:
If the curve $y=f(x)$ passes through the point (1, e) and satisfies the differential equation $d y=y\left(2+\log _{e} x\right) d x, x>0$, then $f(e)$ is equal to :

(2) $\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{e}^{2}}$
(3) $\mathrm{e}^{2 \mathrm{e}}$
(4) $\mathrm{e}^{2^{\mathrm{c}}}$

steps:
$\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\mathrm{y}(2+\ell \mathrm{nx})$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\int \frac{d y}{y}=\int(2+\ell n x) d x \\
\ell n y=2 x+x \ell n x-x+C \\
\ell n y=x+x \ell n x+C
\end{array}$$

Since it passes through $(1, \mathrm{e})$
$$\begin{array}{l}
1=1+0+C \Rightarrow C=0 \\
\ell n y=x+x \ell n x \\
f(x)=y=e^{x+x \ln x} \\
\Rightarrow f(e)=e^{e+e}=e^{2 e}
\end{array}$$

$$\begin{array}{l}

=6((n+1)-n)\left((n+1)^{2}+n^{2}+n(n+1)\right) \\

29. The position of an object having mass 0.1 kg as a function of time t is given as $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{r}}=\left(10 \mathrm{t}^{2} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+5 \mathrm{t}^{3} \hat{\mathrm{j}}\right) \mathrm{m}$. At $\mathrm{t}=1 \mathrm{~s}$, which of the following statements are correct?
A. The linear momentum $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{p}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+1.5 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \mathrm{kg} . \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
B. The force acting on the object $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{F}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}) \mathrm{N}$.
C. The angular momentum of the object about its origin $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{L}}=15 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{J}$ s.
D. The torque acting on the object about its origin $\vec{\tau}=20 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \mathrm{Nm}$.

Choose the correct answer from the option given below.
(1) A, B and C only
(2) B, C and D only
(3) A, C and D only
(4) A, B and D only

Ans. (4)
Sol. Given $\vec{r}=10 t^{2} \hat{i}+5 t^{3} \hat{j} \Rightarrow \vec{r}_{t=1}=10 \hat{i}+5 \hat{j}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\vec{v}=\frac{d \vec{r}}{d t}=20 t \hat{i}+15 t^{2} \hat{j} \Rightarrow \vec{v}_{t=1 s e c}=20 \hat{i}+15 \hat{j} \\
\vec{a}=\frac{d^{2} \vec{r}}{d t^{2}}=20 \hat{i}+30 t \hat{j} \Rightarrow \vec{a}_{t=1 s e c}=20 \hat{i}+30 \hat{j} \\
\therefore \vec{P}=m \vec{v}=2 \hat{i}+1.5 \hat{j} \\
\vec{F}=m \vec{a}=2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j} \\
\vec{\tau}=\vec{r} \times \vec{F}=20 \hat{k} \\
\vec{L}=\vec{r} \times \vec{P}=5 \hat{k}
\end{array}$$
30. A planet $\left(\mathrm{P}_{1}\right)$ is moving around the star of mass 2M in the orbit of radius R . Another planet $\left(\mathrm{P}_{2}\right)$ is moving around another star of mass 4M in a orbit of radius 2R. Ratio of time periods of revolution of $P_{2}$ and $P_{1}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(1) $\frac{1}{2}$
(2) 2
(3) 4
(4) $\frac{1}{4}$

Ans. (2)
Sol. From Kepler's law,
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{T}^{2}=\frac{4 \pi^{2}}{\mathrm{GM}_{\mathrm{S}}} \mathrm{r}^{3} \\
\therefore \mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{1}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{\mathrm{G}(2 \mathrm{M})}} \mathrm{R}^{3 / 2} \\
\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=\frac{2 \pi}{\sqrt{\mathrm{G}(4 \mathrm{M})}}(2 \mathrm{R})^{3 / 2} \\
\therefore \frac{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}}{\mathrm{~T}_{\mathrm{P}_{1}}}=\frac{(2)^{3 / 2}}{\sqrt{4}} \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}}{2}=2
\end{array}$$
31. A particle is rotating in a circular path and at any instant its motion can be described as $\theta=\frac{5 \mathrm{t}^{4}}{40}-\frac{\mathrm{t}^{3}}{3}$. The angular acceleration of the particle after 10 seconds is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.
(1) 150
(2) 120
(3) 130
(4) 170

Ans. (3)
Sol. $\theta=\frac{5 t^{4}}{40}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{d} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{5}{40}\left(4 \mathrm{t}^{3}\right)-\frac{3 \mathrm{t}^{2}}{3}=\frac{\mathrm{t}^{3}}{2}-\mathrm{t}^{2} \\
\alpha=\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2} \theta}{\mathrm{dt}^{2}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{t}^{2}}{2}-2 \mathrm{t} \\
\text { at } \mathrm{t}=10 \\
\alpha=\frac{3}{2}(10)^{2}-2 \times 10=130 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}^{2}
\end{array}$$

32. A parallel plate air capacitor has a capacitance C. When it is half filled as show in figure with a dielectric constant $\mathrm{K}=5$, the percentage increase in the capacitance is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(1) 33.34
(2) 66.67
(3) 200
(4) 400

Ans. (2)
Sol. Initial capacitance
$$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{i}}=\frac{\mathrm{A} \in_{0}}{\mathrm{~d}}=\mathrm{C}$$

Final capacitance
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{C}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{A} \epsilon_{0} \times 5}{\frac{\mathrm{~d}}{2}}=10 \mathrm{C} \\
\mathrm{C}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{A} \epsilon_{0}}{\frac{\mathrm{~d}}{2}}=2 \mathrm{C} \\
\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{1} \mathrm{C}_{2}}{\mathrm{C}_{1}+\mathrm{C}_{2}}=\frac{10 \times 2}{10+2} \mathrm{C}=\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{C} \\
\% \text { increase }=\frac{\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{C}} \times 100=66.67
\end{array}$$
33. Heat is supplied to a diatomic gas at constant pressure. Then the ratio of $\Delta \mathrm{Q}: \Delta \mathrm{U}: \Delta \mathrm{W}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(1) 2 : 3 : 5
(2) 5 : 3 : 2
(3) 2 : 5 : 7
(4) $7: 5: 2$
Ans. (4)

Sol. $\Delta \mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{P}}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{P}} \Delta \mathrm{T}=\frac{7}{2} \mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{T}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{~T}=\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{nR} \Delta \mathrm{~T} \\

\Delta \mathrm{Q}: \Delta \mathrm{U}: \mathrm{W}:: 7: 5: 2

34. Two charged conducting spheres $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ of radii 8 cm and 18 cm are connected to each other by a wire. After equilibrium is established, the ratio of electric fields on $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ spheres are $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 1}$ and $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 2}$ respectively. The value of $\frac{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 1}}{\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{S} 2}}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ .
(1) $\frac{3}{2}$
(2) $\frac{2}{3}$
(3) $\frac{4}{9}$
(4) $\frac{9}{4}$

Ans. (4)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
V_{1}=V_{2} \\
\frac{k Q_{1}}{8}=\frac{k Q_{2}}{18} \quad\left\{V_{\text {surface }}=\frac{k Q}{R}\right\} \\
\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}=\frac{4}{9} \\
\frac{E_{S_{1}}}{E_{S_{2}}}=\frac{k Q_{1}}{r_{1}^{2}} \frac{r_{2}^{2}}{k Q_{2}}\left\{E_{\text {surface }}=\frac{k Q}{R^{2}}\right\} \\
=\frac{Q_{1}}{Q_{2}}\left(\frac{r_{2}}{r_{1}}\right)^{2}=\frac{4}{9} \times\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{2}=\frac{9}{4}
\end{array}$$
